newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 7.0/8.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 7.0/8.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money eased to 7.0/8.0 percent from 11.0/12.0 percent on Monday morning.
Dealers said liquidity was ample on central bank supply of 318 billion rupiah and further transfers of civil servants' salaries.
One local bank dealer said ample short-term funds drove longer-term rates lower. One- and three-month money were last given at 13.0 percent and 13.75 percent, respectively.
He said operators were geting cautious because of the approaching month-end factor.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 10.82 percent, compared with 6.49 percent on Wednesday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable in the morning, but there were no trades recorded yet.
